title: Cognition nears $1B round at $47B valuation — nearly double May's mark
subtitle: The maker of the Devin engineering agent is closing a raise at roughly $47 billion after fielding nearly $10 billion in demand. Annualized revenue has crossed $900 million in four months.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Cognition AI, the maker of the Devin autonomous engineering agent, is set to close a roughly $1 billion funding round at about a $47 billion post-money valuation, Bloomberg reported on September 2. The company received close to $10 billion in investor interest for the round, and the final size may exceed the target. Terms are still being negotiated.

The valuation ramp is the story. Cognition raised $1 billion in May at a $26 billion valuation and $10.2 billion in September 2025 — a roughly 4.5x jump in twelve months and near-double in four. The company reports annualized revenue has climbed from $492 million in May to more than $900 million now, which is what investors are effectively underwriting: the assumption that agentic coding tools are moving from side-of-desk tooling to core developer surface faster than the market currently prices.

The round sits in a wider pattern. Global venture funding hit a record $510 billion in H1 2026 per Crunchbase, and OpenAI and Anthropic alone took 43% of it. Coding-agent companies have been the second concentration zone — SpaceX's Cursor acquisition, Lovable's Series C, Windsurf's rise before its GPT-5-era stall — because they are the clearest place where an agent gets paid per unit of work it completes rather than per query.

For learners: watch what Devin is actually shipping into production, not the valuation. A doubling in ARR while headcount stays small is the shape of a real product-market fit; a doubling driven by a handful of large enterprise pilots that renew at lower rates is the shape of a hype cycle. The next disclosure — customer counts, retention, revenue per developer seat — will tell you which one this is.
